clip_hygiene.defect: the idle clip carried a constant Hips SCALE of 1.176471 = 20/17 exactly -- a 1.70 m source retargeted to a 2.00 m target -- on a rig that is 1.85 m. Hips is the skeleton root, so the whole character was 17.6% bigger whenever he stood still. Present in Meshy's output and carried through T8 and D2 untouched; nb_t8/artifacts/T8-barbarian.glb carried the same defect and was patched the same way on 2026-09-29 (its own offset measured independently from its own feet: -0.17987 m, matching to five decimals); the exporter also neutralises it on the way past, so a rebuild from a fresh Meshy clip is clean too.

armed_carry.complaint: Matt: the axe "waffles back and forth awkwardly.. not the way someone should hold a weapon", and "the axe is better when idling."
armed_carry.cause: the Meshy walk and run are UNARMED motion. A free hand counter-rotates against the forearm through the stride -- life on an empty hand, flop on a rigid 0.8 m axe. Nothing in those clips treats the left arm as holding a shield either.
armed_carry.fix: new clips walk_armed / run_armed: the wrist joint slerped 95% toward the IDLE's mean carry angle, per frame, both arms. walk and run are left untouched for an unarmed barbarian.
armed_carry.why_not_a_layer: shield_carry_L is a static two-frame pose, so it works as a layer. A wrist lock depends on where the forearm is on that frame, so it is per-frame data that a static pose layer cannot express at all.

measured.instrument: wrist rotation in the forearm's frame, deg/s p95 and direction reversals per cycle

final.why_per_clip: one alpha cannot serve all four: they start from different baselines. walk_armed is the awkward one -- its RATE is already inside the 40-70 band at alpha 0 and its THREE reversals are the defect, so any lock that fixes the reversals pushes the rate below the band. Reversals win; they are the complaint metric.
final.previous: alpha 0.95 everywhere, which put walk_armed at 3.4 deg/s -- a weld

shield_grip_defect.finding: the fist sits 0.4599 m from the boss = 109.4% of the shield radius (0.4204 m). His hand is OFF THE DISC, past the rim. There is no grip, exactly as Matt said.
shield_grip_defect.how_it_happened: the D2 socket sweep optimised ONE objective -- shield vertices inside the torso -- and a placement holding the disc at arm's length with its RIM near the hand scores perfectly on it. Nothing asked whether the hand was on the grip. Then R-C9-71 measured "grip bar to left fist min 0.0013 m" and called the grip closed: a TRUE number for the nearest shield surface, which was the rim. A nearest-surface distance cannot say WHICH surface.
